title: VDJ006 for Injection in Healthy Subjects
off: A Phase I, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center, Single and Multiple Ascending Intravenous Infusion Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Immunogenicity of VDJ006 for Injection in Healthy Subjects
summary:
This first-in-human, single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase I dose-escalation trial evaluates the tolerability, safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and immunogenicity of injectable VDJ006 (a long-acting IL-1 receptor antagonist) given by intravenous infusion to healthy Chinese subjects. It includes a single-ascending-dose (SAD) part with 28 subjects across five cohorts (1, 2, 6, 9, 12 mg/kg) and a multiple-ascending-dose (MAD) part with 16 subjects across two cohorts (6, 9 mg/kg) receiving weekly IV infusion for 4 weeks, with dose escalation governed by predefined CTCAE 6.0 stopping rules.

The primary objective is to assess the safety and tolerability of single and multiple VDJ006 doses; secondary objectives are to characterize its PK profile and immunogenicity (anti-drug and neutralizing antibodies). The study targets cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes (CAPS), an IL-1β-driven autoinflammatory disease for which VDJ006 offers a novel, long-acting IL-1 blockade option.
desc:
VDJ006 is a domestically developed Class 1 innovative biologic-an injectable recombinant human IL-1RN-Fc fusion protein produced in CHO cells-that tightly binds IL-1R1 to block IL-1α/β signaling, with markedly enhanced IL-1R1 affinity versus wild-type IL-1RN. Its target, CAPS, is a rare NLRP3-mutation autoinflammatory disease (FCAS, MWS, NOMID/CINCA subtypes) causing recurrent multi-system inflammation, hearing loss, and amyloidosis; IL-1 inhibitors are standard of care, but current domestic options (anakinra, rilonacept) require frequent dosing, supporting development of a long-acting agent. Nonclinical studies showed no major CNS/respiratory/cardiovascular effects, MTD \> 300 mg/kg, NOAEL of 300 mg/kg (rat) and 150 mg/kg (monkey) over 4-week repeat dosing, approximately dose-proportional PK (half-life \~20-27 h), and species-dependent immunogenicity not directly predictive of humans.

The trial enrolls 44 healthy adults (18-55 years; BMI 19-28; normal screening) randomized to VDJ006 or placebo, with escalating doses (SAD: 1:1 at 1-2 mg/kg, 3:1 at 6-12 mg/kg; MAD: 3:1 at 6-9 mg/kg, Q1W × 4). A Safety Review Committee oversees escalation, requiring ≥14 days between cohorts and D15 safety clearance; stopping rules trigger on defined drug-related AE thresholds, defining the MTD as the dose below the first stopping event. Assessments include adverse events, vital signs, labs, ECG, serum VDJ006 concentration (PK: Cmax, AUC, t1/2, etc.), and anti-drug antibody testing, with descriptive and non-compartmental statistical analysis; SAD lasts 71 days and MAD 92 days.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Has signed the informed consent form and is able to complete the trial in accordance with the protocol.
* Aged ≥ 18 and ≤ 55 years (as of the date of informed consent signing); female body weight ≥ 45.0 kg, male body weight ≥ 50.0 kg; body mass index (BMI) between 19.0 and 28.0 kg/m² (BMI = weight \[kg\] / height² \[m²\]), inclusive of the boundaries.
* Medical history, physical examination, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, clinical laboratory tests, and all other trial-related examinations performed prior to enrollment are all normal or show clinically insignificant mild abnormalities, as judged eligible by the clinical investigator.
* Women of childbearing potential have a negative serum pregnancy test, and the subject or their spouse uses appropriate and effective contraceptive measures from the trial period through 6 months after dosing (e.g., abstinence, intrauterine device, and double-barrier method such as condom plus diaphragm).

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of severe systemic disease (including cardiovascular, digestive, hematologic, respiratory, etc.), psychiatric disorder, or drug dependence.
* Any definite food or drug allergy; or, in the investigator's judgment, likely to be allergic to VDJ006 or any of its components.
* Prior definite malignancy, neurological or psychiatric disorder (including epilepsy or dementia), history of heart failure, or immunodeficiency/immunosuppressive disease; or major surgery within 6 months prior to randomization.
* Presence of severe bleeding factors that impair venous blood collection, or inability/unwillingness to undergo venous puncture.
* Vaccination within 3 months prior to randomization, or planned vaccination during the study period.
* Prior treatment with anti-IL-1 or its receptor targeted drugs or other monoclonal antibody therapies; or use of any biologic agent within 12 months prior to randomization or currently in use.
* Participation in another clinical trial and receipt of study drug within 3 months prior to randomization.
* Whole blood, component blood donation, or major blood loss (\>400 mL) within 3 months prior to randomization.
* Active bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic infection within 4 weeks prior to dosing, or any infection event requiring systemic anti-infective therapy.
* Use of any prescription drug, over-the-counter drug, vitamin product, or herbal medicine within 2 weeks prior to first dosing.
* History of drug abuse within 1 year prior to screening, or positive urine drug screen.
* Alcohol abuse or frequent alcohol consumption within 3 months prior to randomization (i.e., \>14 units of alcohol per week: 14 bottles of 360 mL beer, or 630 mL of 40% alcohol liquor, or 2100 mL wine), or positive breath alcohol test.
* Average daily smoking \> 5 cigarettes within 3 months prior to first dosing, or inability to discontinue any tobacco products during the trial.
* Daily excessive consumption of tea, coffee, and/or caffeinated beverages (\>8 cups per day; 1 cup = 250 mL).
* Positive interferon-gamma release assay (T-SPOT.TB).
* Positive for any of the following: HIV antibody (HIV-Ab), Treponema pallidum antibody (TP-Ab), hepatitis C virus antibody (HCV-Ab), or hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).
* Clinically significant abnormal results for rheumatoid factor (RF), anti-double-stranded DNA antibody (anti-dsDNA), antinuclear antibody (ANA), or anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP).
* Planned surgery during the trial (including cosmetic, dental, or oral surgery), or planned participation in strenuous exercise (including contact or collision sports).
* Planned blood donation during the trial; or planned use of any biologic agent within 3 months after study drug administration.
* Planned pregnancy within 6 months after study drug administration, or planned sperm/egg donation within 6 months after study drug administration.
* Deemed unsuitable for enrollment by the investigator, or unlikely to complete the trial for other reasons.
* For female subjects, in addition to the above, exclusion also applies if any of the following conditions are met:

Use of oral contraceptives within 30 days prior to the trial, or planned use during the trial;Use of long-acting estrogen or progesterone injectables or implants within 6 months prior to the trial, or planned use during the trial;Unprotected sexual intercourse with a partner within 14 days prior to the trial;Pregnant or lactating women.

x.titre: VDJ006, antagoniste long de l'IL-1, chez des volontaires sains : tolérance et pharmacocinétique
x.question: Le VDJ006 en perfusion intraveineuse, dose unique ou répétée, est-il bien toléré chez des volontaires sains ?
x.contexte:
Les syndromes périodiques associés à la cryopyrine (CAPS) sont des maladies auto-inflammatoires rares liées à des mutations activatrices de NLRP3, qui entraînent une surproduction d'IL-1β. Ils comprennent le syndrome familial auto-inflammatoire au froid, le syndrome de Muckle-Wells et la maladie CINCA/NOMID, avec des poussées inflammatoires multisystémiques, une surdité et un risque d'amylose.

Le blocage de l'IL-1 est le traitement de référence, avec l'anakinra, le rilonacept et le canakinumab. Les molécules à demi-vie courte imposent des injections fréquentes, d'où l'intérêt d'un antagoniste à action prolongée.

Le VDJ006 est une protéine de fusion IL-1RN-Fc recombinante, issue de Beijing VDJBio, qui se lie à IL-1R1 avec une affinité accrue par rapport à l'antagoniste naturel et bloque la signalisation de l'IL-1α et de l'IL-1β. Les études précliniques n'ont pas montré d'effet notable sur les systèmes nerveux central, respiratoire et cardiovasculaire.

Cet essai de phase 1, randomisé, en double aveugle et contre placebo, est mené dans un centre en Chine chez 44 adultes sains. Une partie à dose unique croissante (1 à 12 mg/kg, 28 participants) est suivie d'une partie à doses répétées (6 et 9 mg/kg, une perfusion par semaine pendant 4 semaines, 16 participants). Un comité de sécurité encadre les paliers de dose. Les critères principaux portent sur la sécurité et la tolérance, la pharmacocinétique et l'immunogénicité étant secondaires.
x.interet: Il s'agit d'une première administration chez l'humain, sans bénéfice clinique attendu pour les participants. Il pourrait préparer le développement d'un anti-IL-1 à action prolongée dans les CAPS.
x.profil: Des adultes sains de 18 à 55 ans.
inclusion: Âge de 18 à 55 ans, poids ≥ 45 kg (femmes) ou ≥ 50 kg (hommes)
Examen clinique, ECG, radiographie thoracique et biologie normaux ou sans anomalie significative
Contraception efficace jusqu'à 6 mois après l'administration
exclusion: Infection active ou nécessitant un anti-infectieux dans les 4 semaines
Sérologies VIH, syphilis, VHC ou antigène HBs positifs, ou test de la tuberculose positif
Participation à un autre essai ou don de sang important dans les 3 mois
Médicament, vitamine ou plante prise dans les 2 semaines précédant la première dose
Abus d'alcool ou de drogues, tabagisme > 5 cigarettes par jour

bras.traitement: Perfusion IV : dose unique de 1, 2, 6, 9 ou 12 mg/kg, ou 6 ou 9 mg/kg une fois par semaine pendant 4 semaines
Placebo en perfusion IV, selon le même schéma

x.critere: Événements indésirables et paramètres de sécurité (examen clinique, ECG, constantes, biologie) jusqu'au jour 57 (dose unique) ou 78 (doses répétées).
